claim.quote: The technique is used to detect TeV emission from the Crab nebula.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal reference as printed on the arXiv page: Astrophys.J.595:803-811,2003.

key_value_text.value: Crab flux 2.68 (+-0.42 stat +-1.4 sys) x 10^-7 (E/1 TeV)^-2.59 m^-2 s^-1 TeV^-1, spectral index assumed from HEGRA

name: Milagro observes the Crab Nebula with a new background-rejection technique
notes: The abstract gives no significance, so none is recorded; the 17 sigma Crab detection over the experiment's lifetime is from the later paper arXiv:1110.0409.

summary.plain: Milagro, an air-shower array, found a way to tell gamma-ray showers from the far more numerous cosmic-ray showers and used it to detect TeV gamma rays from the Crab Nebula.
summary.technical: A method to separate hadronic from electromagnetic air showers in Milagro, based on the ability to detect the energetic particles in an extensive air shower, is used to detect TeV emission from the Crab Nebula; the Crab flux is estimated with the spectral index assumed from HEGRA.

title: Observation of TeV Gamma Rays from the Crab Nebula with Milagro Using a New Background Rejection Technique
why_it_matters: The abstract says that until then no background-rejection method had been used successfully in an air-shower array to detect a source of TeV gamma rays.
